{{Use dmy dates|date=March 2014}}
[[Statistics]] is the theory and application of [[mathematics]] to the [[scientific method]] including hypothesis generation, [[experimental design]], [[Sampling (statistics)|sampling]], [[data collection]], [[Summary statistics|data summarization]], [[Estimator|estimation]], [[prediction]] and [[statistical inference|inference]] from those results to the [[statistical population|population]] from which the experimental sample was drawn. [[Statistician]]s are skilled people who thus apply statistical methods. [[List of statisticians|Hundreds of statisticians are notable]]. This article lists statisticians who have been especially instrumental in the development of [[mathematical statistics|theoretical]] and [[applied statistics]].

| [[William Playfair|Playfair, William]] || Scottish || 1759 || 1823 ||  Pioneer of [[statistical graphics]] ||

| [[Adolphe Quetelet|Quetelet, Adolphe]] || Belgian || 1796 || 1874 ||  Pioneered the use of probability and statistics in the [[social sciences]] ||

|- valign="top"
| [[Francis Galton|Galton, Francis]] || English || 1822 || 1911 ||  Invented the concepts of [[standard deviation]], [[correlation]], [[Regression analysis|regression]] || <ref>{{cite web | url = http://www.economics.soton.ac.uk/staff/aldrich/Figures.htm#gal | work = Figures from the History of Probability and Statistics | title = Francis Galton | publisher = [[University of Southampton]] }}</ref><ref>{{cite web | url = http://galton.org/ | title = Sir Francis Galton F.R.S: 1822–1911 }}</ref>
|- valign="top"
| [[Thorvald N. Thiele|Thiele, Thorvald N.]] || Danish || 1838 || 1910 ||  Introduced [[cumulants]] and the term "[[Likelihood function|likelihood]]". Introduced a [[Kalman filter]] in [[time-series]] ||
|- valign="top"
| [[Charles Sanders Peirce|Peirce, Charles Sanders]] || American || 1839 || 1914 ||  Formulated modern statistics in "[[Charles Sanders Peirce bibliography#illus|Illustrations of the Logic of Science]]" (1877–1878) and "[[Charles Sanders Peirce bibliography#SIL|A Theory of Probable Inference]]" (1883). With a [[repeated measures design]], introduced [[blind experiment|blinded]], [[Randomized controlled trial|controlled randomized experiments]] (before [[Ronald A. Fisher|Fisher]]). Invented [[optimal design]] for experiments on gravity, in which he "[[analysis of variance|corrected the means]]". He used [[correlation]], [[smoothing]], and improved the treatment of [[Peirce's criterion|outliers]]. Introduced terms "[[Confidence interval|confidence]]" and "[[Likelihood function|likelihood]]" (before [[Jerzy Neyman|Neyman]] and [[Ronald A. Fisher|Fisher]]). While largely a [[Frequency probability|frequentist]], Peirce's [[possible world semantics]] introduced the "[[propensity]]" theory of probability. See the historical books of [[Stephen Stigler]] ||
|- valign="top"
| [[Francis Ysidro Edgeworth|Edgeworth, Francis Ysidro]] || Irish || 1845 || 1926 ||  Revived [[Exponential family|exponential families]] ([[Laplace transform]]s) in statistics. Extended [[Pierre-Simon Laplace|Laplace]]'s ([[asymptotic analysis|asymptotic]]) theory of [[Maximum likelihood|maximum-likelihood]] estimation. Introduced basic results on [[Fisher information|information]], which were extended and popularized by [[Ronald A. Fisher|R. A. Fisher]] ||

| [[Ronald Fisher|Fisher, Ronald]] || English || 1890 || 1962 ||  Wrote the textbooks and articles that defined the academic discipline of statistics, inspiring the creation of statistics departments at universities throughout the world. ==Founders of departments of statistics==
The role of a department of statistics is discussed in a 1949 article by Harold Hotelling, which helped to spur the creation of many departments of statistics.<ref>{{cite journal|author=Harold Hotelling|title=Golden Oldies: Classic Articles from the World of Statistics and Probability: 'The Place of Statistics in the University'| journal=[[Statistical Science]]| volume=3 |issue=1 |year=1988 |pages=72–83|doi=10.1214/ss/1177013002|author-link=Harold Hotelling|doi-access=free}}</ref>
